views.name: tracks_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tracks.TrackId AS TrackId,
  tracks.Name AS Name,
  tracks.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  albums.Title AS Title,
  albums.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  artists.Name AS Name_Artist,
  tracks.MediaTypeId AS MediaTypeId,
  media_types.Name AS Name_MediaType,
  tracks.GenreId AS GenreId,
  genres.Name AS Name_Genre,
  tracks.Composer AS Composer,
  tracks.Milliseconds AS Milliseconds,
  tracks.Bytes AS Bytes,
  tracks.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice
FROM tracks
LEFT JOIN albums ON tracks.AlbumId = albums.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists ON albums.ArtistId = artists.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN media_types ON tracks.MediaTypeId = media_types.MediaTypeId
LEFT JOIN genres ON tracks.GenreId = genres.GenreId

params.description: Provides one-row-per-track enriched with album, artist, media type and genre attributes to support track-level reporting and composition.
params.when_to_use: Fetch track master data and descriptive attributes (title, artist name, media type, genre) for display or export. | Build track-level analytics (counts, sums, averages) where each row represents a single TrackId as the grain. | Join track attributes onto other datasets (e.g., sales, playlist entries, invoice lines) when you need stable track-level descriptive context before aggregating.
params.output_schema: TrackId: unique identifier of the track (derived from tracks.TrackId) | Name: track name/title (derived from tracks.Name) | AlbumId: foreign key to the album containing the track (derived from tracks.AlbumId) | Title: album title for the track (derived from albums.Title) | ArtistId: artist id associated with the album (derived from albums.ArtistId) | Name_Artist: artist name (derived from artists.Name) | MediaTypeId: foreign key to the media type of the track (derived from tracks.MediaTypeId) | Name_MediaType: media type name (derived from media_types.Name) | GenreId: foreign key to the genre of the track (derived from tracks.GenreId) | Name_Genre: genre name (derived from genres.Name) | Composer: composer text for the track (derived from tracks.Composer) | Milliseconds: duration of the track in milliseconds (derived from tracks.Milliseconds) | Bytes: file size in bytes (derived from tracks.Bytes) | UnitPrice: unit price for the track (derived from tracks.UnitPrice)
params.grounded_columns: tracks.TrackId | tracks.Name | tracks.AlbumId | albums.Title | albums.ArtistId | artists.Name | tracks.MediaTypeId | media_types.Name | tracks.GenreId | genres.Name | tracks.Composer | tracks.Milliseconds | tracks.Bytes | tracks.UnitPrice
params.metric: This view is strictly at the row-grain (TrackId) and exposes no aggregated metrics. All numeric fields are passthrough base columns, not aggregates. | Milliseconds = tracks.Milliseconds | Bytes = tracks.Bytes | UnitPrice = tracks.UnitPrice
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to albums (or the albums base/view) on tracks_enriched.AlbumId = albums.AlbumId — safe because albums is one-row-per-AlbumId and this view is one-row-per-TrackId; joining adds album attributes without duplicating track rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to artists (or an artists base/view) on tracks_enriched.ArtistId = artists.ArtistId — safe provided ArtistId was populated from albums.ArtistId; artists is one-row-per-ArtistId so measures on tracks_enriched are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to media_types on tracks_enriched.MediaTypeId = media_types.MediaTypeId — safe because media_types is one-row-per-MediaTypeId. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to genres on tracks_enriched.GenreId = genres.GenreId — safe because genres is one-row-per-GenreId. | do NOT join directly (one-to-many) to invoice_lines_enriched or any invoice line table/view without re-aggregating invoice_lines first, because invoice_lines_enriched contains multiple rows per TrackId (sales lines) and joining it directly will multiply track-level rows and inflate any per-track numeric measures (Milliseconds, Bytes, UnitPrice are row attributes and would be duplicated). Instead, aggregate invoice_lines_enriched (e.g., SUM(Quantity), SUM(LineTotal) grouped by TrackId) and then join the aggregated invoice metrics to tracks_enriched on TrackId. | do NOT join directly to playlist entries or other many-to-many tables (e.g., a playlist_tracks table) without first aggregating counts by TrackId, because those joins will multiply track rows. | When composing higher-level aggregates (for example, total revenue by genre), aggregate after joining: either (a) aggregate invoice lines to TrackId first, join that aggregation to tracks_enriched and then aggregate by GenreId/Name_Genre, or (b) join tracks_enriched to a pre-aggregated sales-by-track dataset. This ensures measures remain correct and are not double-counted.

views.description: Denormalized track-level catalog: one row per TrackId with track attributes plus album title and artist name, genre name and media type name. Use this as a canonical track catalog for filtering, aggregation, or joining to sales and playlists. | Use for: List tracks with artist/album/genre/media labels; Aggregate track counts or durations by artist/genre/media type; Filter tracks by composer, duration, size, or price before joining to sales or playlists

views.name: invoice_lines_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  invoice_items.InvoiceLineId AS InvoiceLineId,
  invoice_items.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  invoices.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  invoices.InvoiceDate AS InvoiceDate,
  invoices.BillingCountry AS BillingCountry,
  invoice_items.TrackId AS TrackId,
  invoice_items.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice,
  invoice_items.Quantity AS Quantity,
  (invoice_items.UnitPrice * invoice_items.Quantity) AS LineAmount,
  tracks.TrackId AS TrackId_Track,
  tracks.Name AS Name,
  tracks.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  albums.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  artists.Name AS Name_Artist,
  tracks.GenreId AS GenreId,
  genres.Name AS Name_Genre
FROM invoice_items
LEFT JOIN invoices ON invoice_items.InvoiceId = invoices.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN tracks ON invoice_items.TrackId = tracks.TrackId
LEFT JOIN albums ON tracks.AlbumId = albums.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists ON albums.ArtistId = artists.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN genres ON tracks.GenreId = genres.GenreId

params.description: Enriched invoice line-level view that answers questions about individual invoice lines, their amounts, the purchased track and related track/album/artist/genre metadata.
params.when_to_use: Calculate revenue, counts, or averages at the invoice-line grain (InvoiceLineId) or roll up to InvoiceId, CustomerId, TrackId, AlbumId, ArtistId, GenreId. | Filter or slice invoice-line level data by invoice attributes (InvoiceDate, BillingCountry) or track metadata (Name, Artist, Genre). | Join into aggregations that aggregate invoice-line measures (LineAmount, Quantity) without risk of duplication when joined along one-to-one keys described below.
params.output_schema: InvoiceLineId: primary grain of this view; derived from invoice_items.InvoiceLineId (base column). | InvoiceId: invoice_items.InvoiceId (base column) — the invoice that contains the line. | CustomerId: invoices.CustomerId (base column) — customer who owns the invoice (may be NULL if invoice join failed). | InvoiceDate: invoices.InvoiceDate (base column) — date/time of the invoice. | BillingCountry: invoices.BillingCountry (base column) — billing country for the invoice. | TrackId: invoice_items.TrackId (base column) — track sold on this invoice line (may be NULL). | UnitPrice: invoice_items.UnitPrice (base column) — unit price recorded on the invoice line. | Quantity: invoice_items.Quantity (base column) — quantity on the invoice line. | LineAmount: derived measure = invoice_items.UnitPrice * invoice_items.Quantity (expression); represents revenue for this invoice line before tax/discounts. | TrackId_Track: tracks.TrackId (base column) — redundant track id from joined tracks table; equals TrackId when track join exists. | Name: tracks.Name (base column) — track title from tracks table. | AlbumId: tracks.AlbumId (base column) — album id for the track. | ArtistId: albums.ArtistId (base column) — artist id from the album join. | Name_Artist: artists.Name (base column) — artist name from artists table. | GenreId: tracks.GenreId (base column) — genre id from tracks table. | Name_Genre: genres.Name (base column) — genre name from genres table.
params.grounded_columns: invoice_items.InvoiceLineId | invoice_items.InvoiceId | invoice_items.TrackId | invoice_items.UnitPrice | invoice_items.Quantity | invoices.CustomerId | invoices.InvoiceDate | invoices.BillingCountry | tracks.TrackId | tracks.Name | tracks.AlbumId | albums.ArtistId | artists.Name | tracks.GenreId | genres.Name
params.metric: LineAmount = invoice_items.UnitPrice * invoice_items.Quantity (row-level derived measure, not an aggregate). | You may aggregate LineAmount using SUM(LineAmount) to obtain revenue at higher grains (InvoiceId, CustomerId, TrackId, ArtistId, GenreId, etc.). | Quantity (row-level) can be aggregated with SUM(Quantity) for total units sold.
params.composition: Cardinality-safe joins (do NOT duplicate measures): |  - Join to invoices (or invoices_with_customer) on invoice_items.InvoiceId = invoices.InvoiceId — safe because the view already LEFT JOINs invoices 1:1 by InvoiceId; invoices is one-row-per-invoice so aggregating this view by InvoiceId or higher will not duplicate LineAmount when joining on InvoiceId. |  - Join to tracks_enriched or tracks on invoice_items.TrackId = tracks.TrackId — safe because tracks is one-row-per-TrackId; joining on TrackId does not multiply invoice-line rows and therefore does not duplicate LineAmount. |  - Join to albums on tracks.AlbumId = albums.AlbumId (or use album-level views) — safe when joining on AlbumId if albums is one-row-per-AlbumId; do not join to an album-side table that has multiple rows per AlbumId unless you first aggregate that table to one-row-per-AlbumId. |  - Join to artists (or artist-level aggregates) on albums.ArtistId = artists.ArtistId — safe when artist is one-row-per-ArtistId. Joining by ArtistId keeps invoice-line rows unique. |  - Join to genres on tracks.GenreId = genres.GenreId — safe because genres is one-row-per-GenreId. |  | Joins that can duplicate measures (avoid without re-aggregation): |  - Do NOT directly join to any table or view that is one-to-many relative to TrackId, InvoiceId, or InvoiceLineId (for example, a playlist_tracks table that contains multiple playlists per track, or any event/log table keyed to TrackId with multiple rows) without aggregating that table first to one-row-per-TrackId (or the chosen join key). Such joins will multiply invoice-line rows and therefore multiply LineAmount/Quantity. |  - Do NOT join to playlist_track_counts (if it were one-to-many) or other AGG views that are not guaranteed one-row-per-key unless you verify their grain and join on that grain. |  | Guidance for safe composition by aggregation: |  - To get invoice-line metrics at ArtistId: GROUP BY ArtistId and use SUM(LineAmount), SUM(Quantity). You can also join this view to artist_sales_agg only if artist_sales_agg is one-row-per-ArtistId (otherwise aggregate artist_sales_agg before joining). |  - To combine with track_popularity_rank (a RANK view), ensure track_popularity_rank is one-row-per-TrackId (safe) or aggregate it to one-row-per-TrackId before joining; joining on TrackId will not duplicate measures. |  - If you must join to a one-to-many dimension, first aggregate the many-side to the same grain you intend to analyze (e.g., aggregate playlist entries to counts per TrackId) and then join on TrackId to avoid duplicating LineAmount. |  | Summary rule: This view is one-row-per-InvoiceLineId. Any join that preserves that one-row-per-InvoiceLineId cardinality (i.e., joins to one-row-per-key tables on matching keys) is safe. Avoid joining to tables with multiple rows per the join key unless you pre-aggregate to one row per join key.

views.description: Denormalized invoice line items: one row per InvoiceLineId including invoice header info, customer id and invoice date, plus track metadata (via tracks_enriched). Useful for sales analysis at the line level and for joining revenue to track/artist/genre. | Use for: Compute revenue or units sold by track/artist/genre over time; Identify top-selling tracks or artists; Analyze customer purchases by country or customer

views.name: customer_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customers.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  customers.FirstName AS FirstName,
  customers.LastName AS LastName,
  COUNT(DISTINCT invoices.InvoiceId) AS InvoiceCount,
  SUM(invoices.Total) AS TotalSpent,
  COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_items.TrackId) AS DistinctTracksPurchased,
  MAX(invoices.InvoiceDate) AS LastInvoiceDate
FROM customers
LEFT JOIN invoices ON customers.CustomerId = invoices.CustomerId
LEFT JOIN invoice_items ON invoices.InvoiceId = invoice_items.InvoiceId
GROUP BY customers.CustomerId, customers.FirstName, customers.LastName

params.description: Per-customer sales summary: invoice counts, money spent, distinct tracks purchased, and last purchase date for each customer.
params.when_to_use: Get a single-row summary per customer (e.g., customer profile, reporting row for each customer). | Feed customer-level KPIs to dashboards (InvoiceCount, TotalSpent, DistinctTracksPurchased, LastInvoiceDate). | Join customer metrics into higher-level aggregations (e.g., segment-level totals) while preserving correct measures. | Use as the aggregated customer input when composing additional SQL (e.g., cohorting, lifetime value calculations) without re-aggregating invoice/invoice_item detail.
params.output_schema: CustomerId: unique identifier for the customer — derived from customers.CustomerId (base column); this is the view's grain. | FirstName: customer's first name — derived from customers.FirstName (base column); included as a descriptive attribute at the CustomerId grain. | LastName: customer's last name — derived from customers.LastName (base column); included as a descriptive attribute at the CustomerId grain. | InvoiceCount: number of distinct invoices for the customer — derived as COUNT(DISTINCT invoices.InvoiceId) over invoices linked to customers.CustomerId. | TotalSpent: total monetary sum of invoices for the customer — derived as SUM(invoices.Total) over invoices linked to customers.CustomerId. | DistinctTracksPurchased: number of distinct tracks the customer purchased — derived as COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_items.TrackId) across invoice_items for the customer's invoices. | LastInvoiceDate: most recent invoice date for the customer — derived as MAX(invoices.InvoiceDate) across invoices for the customer.
params.grounded_columns: customers.CustomerId | customers.FirstName | customers.LastName | invoices.InvoiceId | invoices.CustomerId | invoices.Total | invoices.InvoiceDate | invoice_items.InvoiceId | invoice_items.TrackId
params.metric: InvoiceCount = COUNT(DISTINCT invoices.InvoiceId)  -- distinct count of invoices per customers.CustomerId | TotalSpent = SUM(invoices.Total)  -- sum of invoice totals for invoices belonging to the customer | DistinctTracksPurchased = COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_items.TrackId)  -- distinct tracks across the customer's invoice items | LastInvoiceDate = MAX(invoices.InvoiceDate)  -- latest invoice date for the customer
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customers (or any customer-dimension view) on CustomerId — safe because this view is one-row-per-CustomerId (the same grain), so measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to invoices_with_customer (JOIN) on CustomerId only to bring additional customer-level attributes if that view is 1:1 per customer; verify invoices_with_customer's grain before joining because if it is invoice-grained you would multiply rows. | do NOT join directly to invoice_lines_enriched (invoice-line or invoice_items grain) or to invoice-level/invoice-item level tables without re-aggregating by CustomerId first — joining a one-row-per-customer aggregated view to one-to-many invoice or invoice_item detail will multiply the aggregated measures (InvoiceCount, TotalSpent, DistinctTracksPurchased) and produce incorrect totals. | do NOT join directly to playlist_track_counts or track_popularity_rank (track- or playlist-grained) without aggregating those tables to customer level first — these are one-to-many relative to customers and will duplicate this view's per-customer measures. | safe composition pattern: if you need to combine customer_summary with another table that is at invoice or invoice_item grain, either (a) aggregate that other table to CustomerId first, then join on CustomerId; or (b) join at detail level (e.g., invoices) and re-aggregate at the desired grain — do not naively inner-join customer_summary to a detail-level table. | example safe join: customer_summary JOIN tracks_enriched_aggregated_by_customer USING (CustomerId) — safe because the right side must be pre-aggregated to one row per CustomerId; the planner must ensure the joined side is 1:1 or aggregated to avoid measure duplication. | note on NULLs and LEFT JOINs: the view uses LEFT JOIN from customers to invoices and invoice_items so customers with no invoices appear with InvoiceCount=0 or NULL for aggregates depending on SQL engine; when composing, treat missing/NULL measures appropriately (coalesce if you require zeros).

views.description: Per-customer aggregates derived from invoices and invoice_items: total spent, number of invoices, number of distinct tracks purchased, and last invoice date. Useful for customer lifetime value, recency/frequency/monetary analyses and customer segmentation. | Use for: Rank customers by total spend or invoice frequency; Identify inactive customers by LastInvoiceDate; Feed RFM segmentation or churn prediction features

views.name: artist_sales_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  artists.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  artists.Name AS Name,
  SUM(invoice_items.UnitPrice * invoice_items.Quantity) AS Revenue,
  SUM(invoice_items.Quantity) AS QuantitySold,
  COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_items.TrackId) AS DistinctTracksSold,
  MIN(invoices.InvoiceDate) AS FirstSaleDate,
  MAX(invoices.InvoiceDate) AS LastSaleDate
FROM invoice_items
LEFT JOIN invoices ON invoice_items.InvoiceId = invoices.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN tracks ON invoice_items.TrackId = tracks.TrackId
LEFT JOIN albums ON tracks.AlbumId = albums.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists ON albums.ArtistId = artists.ArtistId
GROUP BY artists.ArtistId, artists.Name

params.description: Artist-level sales rollup: total revenue, units, distinct tracks sold, and first/last sale dates per artist.
params.when_to_use: Get artist-level sales KPIs (revenue, quantity sold, distinct tracks sold) for reporting or dashboards. | As a building block when composing higher-level queries that need artist sales by artist (e.g., join to artist attributes or rank artists). | To answer time-windowed or filtered sales questions after applying filters that don’t change the artist grain (e.g., restrict invoices by date before aggregating).
params.output_schema: ArtistId: unique identifier for the artist, from artists.ArtistId (grouping key for this view). | Name: artist display name, from artists.Name (included for convenience and grouped by in the view). | Revenue: total revenue for the artist calculated as SUM(invoice_items.UnitPrice * invoice_items.Quantity) (derived from invoice_items.UnitPrice and invoice_items.Quantity joined to invoices/invoice_items). | QuantitySold: total quantity of invoice items sold for the artist, SUM(invoice_items.Quantity) (derived from invoice_items.Quantity). | DistinctTracksSold: count of distinct tracks sold for the artist, COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_items.TrackId) (derived from invoice_items.TrackId). | FirstSaleDate: earliest invoice date for the artist, MIN(invoices.InvoiceDate) (derived from invoices.InvoiceDate). | LastSaleDate: latest invoice date for the artist, MAX(invoices.InvoiceDate) (derived from invoices.InvoiceDate).
params.grounded_columns: invoice_items.UnitPrice | invoice_items.Quantity | invoice_items.TrackId | invoice_items.InvoiceId | invoices.InvoiceDate | invoices.InvoiceId | tracks.TrackId | tracks.AlbumId | albums.AlbumId | albums.ArtistId | artists.ArtistId | artists.Name
params.metric: Revenue = SUM(invoice_items.UnitPrice * invoice_items.Quantity) | QuantitySold = SUM(invoice_items.Quantity) | DistinctTracksSold = COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_items.TrackId) | FirstSaleDate = MIN(invoices.InvoiceDate) | LastSaleDate = MAX(invoices.InvoiceDate)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to an artists dimension (artists) on ArtistId — safe because this view is one row per ArtistId, so joining back to artists on artists.ArtistId = artist_sales_agg.ArtistId will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tracks_enriched (JOIN) on ArtistId — only safe if tracks_enriched is at one-row-per-ArtistId grain (it is a JOIN view; verify its grain). If tracks_enriched is one-row-per-track (likely), DO NOT join directly without re-aggregation because that would multiply artist_sales_agg measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to invoices_with_customer (JOIN) on nothing by default — not safe to join invoices_with_customer directly to this artist-aggregated view because invoices_with_customer is at invoice-level (one-to-many to artists through invoice_items); such a join would duplicate artist metrics. Instead: either (a) re-aggregate invoices_with_customer to artist grain (e.g., aggregate invoice metrics by ArtistId) before joining, or (b) join artist_sales_agg to invoices_with_customer only after reducing invoices_with_customer to one row per ArtistId. | do NOT join to invoice_lines_enriched (JOIN) directly without re-aggregation — invoice_lines_enriched is invoice-item level (one-to-many to artist), and joining it will multiply Revenue/QuantitySold/DistinctTracksSold unless you re-aggregate the joined result back to ArtistId. | do NOT join to sibling AGG views that are at a different grain without aligning grain first — for example, joining to playlist_track_counts (AGG) is safe only if playlist_track_counts is one-row-per-ArtistId. If it is one-row-per-playlist, joining without aggregation will multiply rows. | safe composition pattern: to enrich this view with additional dimensions that are many-to-one into ArtistId (attributes where each ArtistId has exactly one row), join directly on ArtistId — measures remain correct. | safe composition pattern: to combine with other detailed-level tables/views (tracks, invoice lines, invoices), first filter/re-aggregate those tables to ArtistId (using the same aggregation semantics or compatible metrics) and then join on ArtistId to avoid measure duplication. | explanatory note for planner: this view's measures are aggregated over invoice_items joined through tracks->albums->artists and grouped by artists.ArtistId. Any join that preserves the one-row-per-ArtistId cardinality (i.e., joining to a dimension with unique ArtistId) will not change the measures. Any join to a table/view that is one-to-many to ArtistId will multiply the aggregated measures unless that table/view is pre-aggregated to ArtistId or the planner re-aggregates after the join.

views.description: Artist-level sales aggregates computed from invoice lines joined to track->album->artist: total revenue, total quantity sold, distinct tracks sold, and first/last sale date per artist. Useful for comparing artist performance over time. | Use for: List top-earning artists; Track revenue trajectory per artist between dates; Compare quantity vs revenue across artists

views.name: track_popularity_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.TrackId AS TrackId,
  t.Name AS Name,
  COALESCE(SUM(ii.Quantity), 0) AS QuantitySold,
  COALESCE(SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity), 0) AS Revenue,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(ii.Quantity),0) DESC) AS QuantityRank,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity),0) DESC) AS RevenueRank
FROM tracks t
LEFT JOIN invoice_items ii ON t.TrackId = ii.TrackId
GROUP BY t.TrackId, t.Name
ORDER BY Revenue DESC

params.description: Ranks tracks by total quantity sold and total revenue, returning per-track sales totals and rank positions.
params.when_to_use: Find top-selling tracks by units sold or by revenue. | Power leaderboards showing track sales rank (by quantity or revenue). | Compose with track-level dimensions (artist, genre, album) to compare or filter ranked tracks without re-aggregating sales. | Use as a stable, per-track aggregated source when building reports that need track sales totals plus rank metrics.
params.output_schema: TrackId: unique identifier of the track (tracks.TrackId). This is the grouping/grain key for the view. | Name: track name/title (tracks.Name) as provided in the tracks table. Descriptive string, non-aggregated. | QuantitySold: total units sold for the track; derived as COALESCE(SUM(invoice_items.Quantity), 0). Aggregation over invoice_items rows linked to the track. | Revenue: total revenue for the track; derived as COALESCE(SUM(invoice_items.UnitPrice * invoice_items.Quantity), 0). Aggregation over invoice_items rows linked to the track. | QuantityRank: rank position of the track when ordering by QuantitySold descending; derived using RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(invoice_items.Quantity),0) DESC). Ties receive the same rank (standard SQL RANK semantics). | RevenueRank: rank position of the track when ordering by Revenue descending; derived using RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(invoice_items.UnitPrice * invoice_items.Quantity),0) DESC). Ties receive the same rank.
params.metric: QuantitySold = COALESCE(SUM(invoice_items.Quantity), 0) -- per-track SUM of invoice_items.Quantity after LEFT JOIN from tracks to invoice_items | Revenue = COALESCE(SUM(invoice_items.UnitPrice * invoice_items.Quantity), 0) -- per-track SUM of line-level revenue (UnitPrice * Quantity) | QuantityRank = RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(invoice_items.Quantity),0) DESC) -- window rank computed over the grouped per-track QuantitySold | RevenueRank = RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(invoice_items.UnitPrice * invoice_items.Quantity),0) DESC) -- window rank computed over the grouped per-track Revenue
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tracks_enriched on TrackId — safe because this view is one-row-per-TrackId (grain = TrackId). Joining on TrackId to a one-row-per-track dimension/view will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to artist or album-level single-row-per-track views (if available) on TrackId — safe because those are 1:1 with tracks and will not multiply aggregates. | do NOT join directly to invoice_items (or any other invoice-line level table) without re-aggregation: invoice_items is one-to-many relative to this view's TrackId; joining it back will duplicate QuantitySold and Revenue measures unless you first aggregate invoice_items to track-level or use DISTINCT keys. Always re-aggregate invoice-level data before joining. | do NOT join to playlist_track_counts (if it is one-to-many per track) without checking cardinality: if playlist_track_counts is aggregated to one-row-per-track (counts), it is safe to join on TrackId; if it contains multiple rows per track (e.g., per-playlist entries), joining will multiply measures. Ensure the other side is also one-row-per-TrackId. | when composing higher-level aggregates (e.g., artist_sales_agg or customer_summary): prefer joining this view to artist_sales_agg on TrackId only if that sibling aggregate is one-row-per-TrackId. If the target is aggregated at artist grain, aggregate this view up to artist first (e.g., SUM(QuantitySold), SUM(Revenue)) rather than joining raw to artist-level rows, to avoid double-counting. | ordering/limits: this view already computes rank and per-track totals; if you join to other dimensions and then filter (e.g., by genre or playlist) to produce a subset ranking, recompute ranks after filtering if you need ranks restricted to the filtered set. The stored QuantityRank/RevenueRank reflect global ranks across the entire tracks table and will be incorrect for filtered subsets unless re-ranked. | null-handling note: tracks with no invoice_items rows will appear with QuantitySold = 0 and Revenue = 0 due to LEFT JOIN + COALESCE; they are included as distinct TrackId rows and have rank positions according to those zero totals.

views.description: Ranked tracks by sales volume and revenue: one row per TrackId with total quantity and revenue and rank columns that order tracks by QuantitySold and Revenue (ties handled by RANK). Useful as a basis for Top-K queries by applying WHERE QuantityRank <= k or RevenueRank <= k downstream. | Use for: Return top-N tracks by units sold or revenue; Compare rank positions across different metrics; Filter top tracks within a genre/artist by joining to tracks_enriched

views.name: playlist_track_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.PlaylistId AS PlaylistId,
  p.Name AS Name,
  COUNT(pt.TrackId) AS TrackCount,
  SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS TotalMilliseconds,
  SUM(t.Bytes) AS TotalBytes
FROM playlists p
LEFT JOIN playlist_track pt ON p.PlaylistId = pt.PlaylistId
LEFT JOIN tracks t ON pt.TrackId = t.TrackId
GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name

params.description: Per-playlist aggregates: number of tracks and summed track duration/size for each playlist.
params.when_to_use: Get counts and totals (milliseconds, bytes) at the playlist level (one row per PlaylistId). | Drive leaderboard or reporting of playlists by track count, total duration, or total size. | As an aggregated building block to join with playlist metadata or customer-facing views without re-aggregating track-level data. | Compose into higher-level joins (e.g., join to customers or invoices) when you need playlist-level measures preserved.
params.output_schema: PlaylistId: the playlist primary key used as the view grain; derived from playlists.PlaylistId | Name: playlist name label; derived from playlists.Name | TrackCount: number of tracks associated with the playlist; derived as COUNT(playlist_track.TrackId) | TotalMilliseconds: sum of track durations (Milliseconds) for all tracks on the playlist; derived as SUM(tracks.Milliseconds) | TotalBytes: sum of track file sizes (Bytes) for all tracks on the playlist; derived as SUM(tracks.Bytes)
params.grounded_columns: playlists.PlaylistId | playlists.Name | playlist_track.TrackId | playlist_track.PlaylistId | tracks.TrackId | tracks.Milliseconds | tracks.Bytes
params.metric: TrackCount = COUNT(playlist_track.TrackId)  -- aggregate counting matching playlist_track rows per PlaylistId (NULL-safe via LEFT JOIN) | TotalMilliseconds = SUM(tracks.Milliseconds)  -- aggregate sum of tracks.Milliseconds for tracks linked to the playlist (NULLs ignored) | TotalBytes = SUM(tracks.Bytes)  -- aggregate sum of tracks.Bytes for tracks linked to the playlist (NULLs ignored)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to playlists (base table) on PlaylistId — safe because this view is one-row-per playlists.PlaylistId; joining back to playlists does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE: join to any 1:1 or many-to-1 dimension keyed by PlaylistId (if such a dim exists) on PlaylistId — safe because this view already has one row per PlaylistId and those joins do not multiply rows. | DO NOT directly join to playlist_track or tracks (one-to-many to this view) without re-aggregation — e.g., joining playlist_track on PlaylistId will multiply TrackCount/TotalMilliseconds/TotalBytes because playlist_track has one row per track. If you must combine with track-level detail, either (a) join and then re-aggregate the combined result or (b) start from track-level views (tracks_enriched) and compute new aggregates at the intended grain. | When joining to sibling aggregated views, ensure keys are compatible: e.g., joining playlist_track_counts (grain=PlaylistId) to customer_summary (grain=CustomerId) is one-to-many from customers to playlists — safe if you want per-playlist context, but be aware customer_summary measures (customer-level) will be duplicated per playlist unless you aggregate or keep them only as dimensions. If you need to preserve both measures, join on PlaylistId only when the other view is also at PlaylistId grain or is a dimension. | Avoid joining to any view/table that is many-to-many with playlists without an intermediate unique key mapping or re-aggregation, because that will incorrectly multiply the aggregated measures in this view. | If you need to build measures that combine playlist aggregates with other aggregates, prefer: (1) join only to row-unique dimensions keyed by PlaylistId, or (2) perform separate aggregations at their native grains and then join those aggregated results at an appropriate grain with explicit combine logic (e.g., sum of playlist totals).

views.description: Per-playlist counts and total duration: one row per PlaylistId giving number of tracks and total milliseconds and total bytes. Useful to rank or filter playlists by size or duration and to join with playlist metadata. | Use for: Find largest or longest playlists; Filter playlists by minimum total duration or track count; Compare playlist sizes across names

views.name: invoices_with_customer
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  invoices.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  invoices.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  customers.FirstName AS FirstName,
  customers.LastName AS LastName,
  customers.Email AS Email,
  invoices.InvoiceDate AS InvoiceDate,
  invoices.BillingCountry AS BillingCountry,
  invoices.Total AS Total
FROM invoices
LEFT JOIN customers ON invoices.CustomerId = customers.CustomerId

params.description: One-row-per-invoice view combining invoice header fields with the invoice's customer attributes (name, email).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve invoice-level details together with customer identity/contact for reporting or UI display (invoice lists, detail pages). | Filter or group invoices by customer attributes (e.g., list invoices for a given customer, country, or email domain) without needing extra joins. | Serve as a base for invoice-level aggregations (e.g., sum of invoice totals) or joins where invoice is the grain.
params.output_schema: InvoiceId: unique invoice identifier — derived from invoices.InvoiceId (base column). | CustomerId: customer identifier on the invoice — derived from invoices.CustomerId (base column). | FirstName: customer's first name — derived from customers.FirstName (base column; may be NULL when no matching customer due to LEFT JOIN). | LastName: customer's last name — derived from customers.LastName (base column; may be NULL when no matching customer due to LEFT JOIN). | Email: customer's email address — derived from customers.Email (base column; may be NULL when no matching customer due to LEFT JOIN). | InvoiceDate: date/time when invoice was created — derived from invoices.InvoiceDate (base column). | BillingCountry: billing country recorded on the invoice — derived from invoices.BillingCountry (base column). | Total: invoice total amount (monetary) — derived from invoices.Total (base column / measure at invoice grain).
params.grounded_columns: invoices.InvoiceId | invoices.CustomerId | invoices.InvoiceDate | invoices.BillingCountry | invoices.Total | customers.CustomerId | customers.FirstName | customers.LastName | customers.Email
params.metric: Total = invoices.Total  -- a base measure stored at the InvoiceId grain (no aggregation in this view).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer_summary on CustomerId — safe because customer_summary is an aggregation at customer grain (one-row-per-customer), so joining invoices_with_customer (one-row-per-invoice) to customer_summary on invoices_with_customer.CustomerId = customer_summary.CustomerId will NOT duplicate invoice rows or the invoices_with_customer.Total measure. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tracks_enriched on no key is provided here — do NOT join invoices_with_customer directly to tracks_enriched because tracks_enriched is a track-level view (likely many tracks) and there is no invoice->track direct key; such joins would either be invalid or would multiply invoice rows if a many relationship exists. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to invoice_lines_enriched only if you intend to drill down to invoice-line detail and you re-aggregate appropriately — invoice_lines_enriched is one-to-many relative to invoices (multiple invoice lines per InvoiceId). Joining invoices_with_customer to invoice_lines_enriched on InvoiceId will multiply invoice rows (one per line). To preserve invoice-level measures you must either: (a) aggregate invoice_lines_enriched back to InvoiceId before joining (e.g., SUM(line_amount) AS lines_total GROUP BY InvoiceId) and then join on InvoiceId, or (b) join and then use GROUP BY invoices_with_customer.InvoiceId to re-aggregate measures such as Total. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to artist_sales_agg, track_popularity_rank, or playlist_track_counts only when joining on keys at compatible grains (e.g., artist_sales_agg by ArtistId, playlist_track_counts by PlaylistId). These are aggregate or rank views at their own grains; joining on those views is safe if you join using the appropriate one-to-one or many-to-one key that does not create duplication of invoice rows. If no direct key exists between invoice and those aggregates, do not join directly. | Do NOT join invoices_with_customer to any raw one-to-many detail table/view (like invoice_lines_enriched or track-level tables) without re-aggregation or grouping first, because invoices_with_customer is one-row-per-InvoiceId and such joins will multiply its Total measure and other invoice-level attributes. Always decide whether you want invoice-level results (keep this view as-is and aggregate details first) or line-level results (start from invoice_lines_enriched and join customer info, aggregating customers if needed).

views.description: Invoice header joined with customer basic info: one row per InvoiceId containing billing fields and customer contact, for use in customer-level or invoice-level reporting. | Use for: Invoice lists with customer contact for outreach; Aggregate invoice totals by country or customer; Filter invoices by date ranges or customer attributes

views.name: tracks_with_album_and_artist
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  te.TrackId AS TrackId,
  te.Name AS TrackName,
  te.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  te.Title AS AlbumTitle,
  te.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  te.Name_Artist AS ArtistName,
  te.GenreId AS GenreId,
  te.Composer AS Composer,
  te.Milliseconds AS Milliseconds,
  te.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice
FROM tracks_enriched te
views.description: Denormalized track rows joined to their album and artist to expose track -> album -> artist relationships and identifiers.

views.name: invoice_items_with_invoice_and_customer_and_track
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  il.InvoiceLineId,
  il.InvoiceId,
  il.CustomerId,
  il.InvoiceDate,
  il.TrackId,
  il.AlbumId,
  il.UnitPrice,
  il.Quantity,
  (il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS LineRevenue
FROM invoice_lines_enriched il
views.description: Invoice line items joined to invoice (to get CustomerId and InvoiceDate) and to track (to get TrackId and AlbumId) exposing raw revenue measure per invoice line.

views.name: artist_revenue_by_tracklines
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  a.Name AS ArtistName,
  COALESCE(SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity), 0.0) AS ArtistTotalRevenue
FROM artists a
LEFT JOIN albums al ON al.ArtistId = a.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN tracks t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
GROUP BY a.ArtistId, a.Name
views.description: Pre-aggregated revenue per artist computed by summing invoice line revenue for tracks that belong to that artist's albums. Keeps artist-level revenue for ranking/top-artist selection.

views.name: invoice_line_track_album_artist
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ii.InvoiceLineId AS InvoiceLineId,
  ii.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  inv.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  t.TrackId AS TrackId,
  t.Name AS TrackName,
  al.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  al.Title AS AlbumTitle,
  ar.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  ar.Name AS ArtistName,
  ii.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice,
  ii.Quantity AS Quantity,
  (ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS LineAmount
FROM invoice_items ii
LEFT JOIN invoices inv ON ii.InvoiceId = inv.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
LEFT JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists ar ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
grain: InvoiceLineId -- one row per invoice_items record (invoice line)
views.description: Denormalized invoice line rows joined to track, album and artist. One row per invoice_items.invoiceLineId (invoice line) with linked track, album and artist identifiers and pricing/quantity values. Useful to compute sales by track/album/artist and to attribute customer spending to artists.

views.name: artist_total_sales_by_invoice_lines
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ie.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  ie.Name_Artist AS ArtistName,
  SUM(ie.UnitPrice * ie.Quantity) AS total_sales
FROM invoice_lines_enriched ie
GROUP BY
  ie.ArtistId,
  ie.Name_Artist
views.description: Total sales aggregated per artist computed from invoice lines (sum of UnitPrice * Quantity). Exposes artist id and name and raw total_sales measure. Useful to rank artists by sales or to filter top/bottom sellers.

views.name: customer_spend_by_artist
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ile.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  ile.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  SUM(ile.UnitPrice * ile.Quantity) AS customer_total_spend,
  COUNT(ile.InvoiceLineId) AS invoice_line_count
FROM invoice_lines_enriched ile
GROUP BY
  ile.CustomerId,
  ile.ArtistId
views.description: Per-customer spending aggregated by artist. For each (CustomerId, ArtistId) pair returns total_spend (sum of UnitPrice * Quantity) and the count of invoice lines. Useful to compute average spending among customers who bought from a given artist.

views.name: customers_with_country
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CustomerId,
  Country
FROM customers
views.description: One row per customer with canonical country and customer identifier; useful for grouping or filtering customers by country.

views.name: invoice_totals_by_customer
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  COUNT(i.InvoiceId) AS customer_invoice_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0.0) AS customer_total_invoiced
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
GROUP BY c.CustomerId
views.description: Per-customer invoice totals: each row is one customer with the sum of their invoice Total values and count of invoices. Keeps raw monetary totals to allow downstream grouping and aggregation by country or other dimensions.

views.name: country_sales_aggregation
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.Country AS Country,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.CustomerId) AS country_customer_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0.0) AS country_total_sales
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
GROUP BY c.Country
views.description: Per-country sales aggregation: for each customer country, compute the number of distinct customers and the total sales amount (sum of invoices.Total for customers in that country). Exposes the country, customer_count, and country_total_sales for downstream statistics like median.

views.name: track_invoice_item_sales
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ii.InvoiceLineId AS InvoiceLineId,
  ii.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  inv.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  ii.TrackId AS TrackId,
  t.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  ii.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice,
  ii.Quantity AS Quantity,
  (ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS LineTotal
FROM invoice_items ii
JOIN invoices inv ON ii.InvoiceId = inv.InvoiceId
JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
views.description: Denormalized rows of invoice line sales joined to tracks and invoices so each row represents a single invoice_item sale of a particular track, including links to the track's album and the invoice's customer.

views.name: album_artist
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  albums.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  albums.Title AS Title,
  albums.ArtistId AS ArtistId
FROM albums
views.description: Mapping of albums to their artist, one row per album, exposing album and artist identifiers and album title.

views.name: artist_sales_by_trackline
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ta.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  ii.InvoiceLineId AS InvoiceLineId,
  ii.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  inv.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  (ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS LineTotal
FROM invoice_items ii
JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
JOIN albums ta ON t.AlbumId = ta.AlbumId
JOIN invoices inv ON ii.InvoiceId = inv.InvoiceId
views.description: Pre-aggregated sales amount per artist per invoice line by attributing each invoice_item line to the track's album artist. One row per artist per invoice line (suitable for summing to get total sales per artist or per customer-by-artist).

views.name: invoice_item_track_album_artist_sales
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ii.InvoiceLineId AS InvoiceLineId,
  ii.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  inv.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  ii.TrackId AS TrackId,
  t.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  a.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  ii.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice,
  ii.Quantity AS Quantity,
  (ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS line_amount
FROM invoice_items ii
JOIN invoices inv ON ii.InvoiceId = inv.InvoiceId
JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
JOIN albums a ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId
WHERE t.AlbumId IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per invoice_item joined to its track, track's album and album's artist, exposing raw sale amount (unitprice*quantity) and relevant ids for aggregations.

views.name: artist_total_album_sales
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  a.Name AS Name,
  COALESCE(SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity), 0.0) AS total_artist_sales
FROM artists a
LEFT JOIN albums al ON al.ArtistId = a.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN tracks t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
WHERE t.AlbumId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY a.ArtistId, a.Name
views.description: Total album sales per artist (summing invoice item line amounts for tracks that belong to albums by that artist). One row per artist with their total sales and name for tie-breaking.

views.name: customers_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CustomerId,
  Country
FROM customers
WHERE Country IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per customer with canonical key and cleaned geographic fields; preserves customer identity and country for grouping and joins.

views.name: invoices_clean
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  invoices.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  invoices.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  invoices.Total AS Total
FROM invoices
WHERE invoices.Total IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per invoice with canonical key and numeric total; excludes invoices where Total is NULL so sums ignore them.

views.name: country_level_sales_from_invoices
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.Country AS Country,
  SUM(i.Total) AS total_sales,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.CustomerId) AS num_customers
FROM customers c
JOIN invoices i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
WHERE c.Country IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY c.Country
views.description: Total sales per customer country computed by summing invoice totals for invoices whose customers are in that country. One row per customers.Country.
